findings.title: Completion Evidence misstates the size of cli_read_output_tests.rs (claims 193 lines; the staged file is 184)
findings.evidence: roadmap/phase-100660-cli-scores-breakdown.md: `| Size | touched files | 247 / 295 / 193 / 387 lines |` and Completion Evidence `116 -> 193 lines`. Measured on the staged blob: `git show :crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read_output_tests.rs | wc -l` -> 184; `git diff --cached --numstat` -> 71 insertions, 3 deletions against the 116-line HEAD file (116 + 71 - 3 = 184). The other three figures are correct: cli_read_render.rs 247, cli_read_render_scores_tests.rs 295, main.rs 387.
findings.requirement_ref: phase-100660 section 9 AC-100660-05 evidence row and Completion Evidence 'Changed components'
findings.recommendation: Correct both places to 184 lines, or re-measure the staged blob with `wc -l` and paste the real number.
findings.resolution: Confirmed by re-measurement: `git show :crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read_output_tests.rs | wc -l` -> 184, and the working-tree file is also 184. Corrected in the phase file. The stale 193 appeared in three places, not two: the AC-100660-05 evidence row, the Quality Gates `Size` row, and the Completion Evidence 'Changed components' cell. All three are now gone; `grep -n 193 roadmap/phase-100660-cli-scores-breakdown.md` returns nothing. The AC row and the Size row no longer hard-code a number list at all: they point at the Quality Gates table, which now lists all eight touched files with their measured counts (247 / 295 / 184 / 387 / 424 / 265 / 405 / 207), each verified with `wc -l` on the working tree after the final edit. The other three original figures were re-measured and are unchanged.

findings.title: The required real-CLI end-to-end check for the breakdown is manual only; no automated test asserts the new text through the spawned binary
findings.evidence: roadmap/phase-100660-cli-scores-breakdown.md section 8 'Required Tests': '- [ ] End-to-end tests (real CLI `recall` text and `--output json`)' is still unticked, as are the other six Required Tests boxes. The existing real-binary harness crates/clio-lib/tests/output_alias_harness.rs:118-121 spawns `clio recall alias -o text` but asserts only `Results for: alias`. The staged in-process test crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read_output_tests.rs:122 uses run_state, not a spawned process. The real CLI run is evidence in the phase file only: I reproduced it with target/debug/clio and a scratch SQLite db and got `scores: final 0.0118  semantic -  keyword 0.000001  reranker -`; the behavior is correct today, but no committed test fails if the binary wiring regresses.
findings.requirement_ref: phase-100660 section 8 Required Tests (end-to-end bullet) and T100660-06
findings.recommendation: Add one assertion in crates/clio-lib/tests/output_alias_harness.rs (or a new `*_test.rs` harness within the 450-line cap) that the spawned binary's recall text contains a `scores: final ` line with `-` for an absent arm and that `-o json` stdout carries no `scores: final` line; then tick the section 8 boxes that hold.
findings.resolution: Reproduced first, as reported: `target/debug/clio remember "terse answers beat verbose replies" --category tool_config --db <scratch>` then `recall terse --output text` printed `scores: final 0.0118  semantic -  keyword 0.000001  reranker -`, `--output json` emitted the payload with no text-view line, and `recall zzz-nothing --output text` printed exactly `no results`. A new harness now makes that a committed test: `crates/clio-lib/tests/recall_text_scores_harness.rs` (207 lines), test `recall_text_shows_the_stage_breakdown_end_to_end`. It spawns the built binary via `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_clio")` for `remember`, then for `recall --output text` and `recall --output json`. It asserts the disclaimer and `[lexical match]`, `semantic -` and `reranker -` with no `<arm> 0` substring, that the `keyword` arm parses, is > 0 and is not equal to its own four-decimal rendering, that the headline `score` and the breakdown `final` agree, that JSON keeps the four score keys with `semantic`/`reranker` null and carries neither `scores: final` nor the disclaimer, and that an empty query prints `no results`. A separate file was used rather than `output_alias_harness.rs` because that file's own header scopes it to the `-o`/`--output` alias contract, and AGENTS.md requires headers to describe the module truthfully. Proven live by two mutations, both reverted (`git diff --stat` on `cli_read_render.rs` is empty afterwards): setting `STAGE_ABSENT` to `0.0000` fails the harness at line 139 with 'semantic shown as a number'; deleting the breakdown push from `render_recall` fails it at line 109 with 'no breakdown line in the recall text'. All seven section 8 Required Tests boxes are now ticked and each names the tests that satisfy it.

findings.title: Phase doc parent-requirement citation is wrong: PR-4 is about snapshot/gist, and requirement.md states no score-calibration rule
findings.evidence: roadmap/phase-100660-cli-scores-breakdown.md:41 cites 'PR-4 / §4.5 (never present a fused/derived score as calibrated)'. requirement.md:128 defines PR-4 as 'Snapshot for truth, gist for flow'; requirement.md §4.5 (lines 207-236) describes the retrieval path with no calibration wording; `grep -i calibrat baseline/requirement.md` returns no matches. Only the §4.9.4.G reference maps to the diagnostic-visibility claim (requirement.md:421, `explain` returns a score/domain/hop trace). The citation predates the implementation and the staged code does not violate any requirement.
findings.recommendation: Fix the Parent Requirement line to cite what exists (for example §4.9.4.G / P12 diagnostic visibility plus §4.5 for the stage values), or record an explicit product decision if the 'relative, not calibrated' disclaimer is meant to be a standing rule.
findings.resolution: Confirmed by re-reading the cited lines: requirement.md:128 defines PR-4 as 'Snapshot for truth, gist for flow'; §4.5 (207-236) step 3 is the dense + lexical/BM25 + graph + rerank description with no calibration wording; `grep -i calibrat baseline/requirement.md` returns zero matches; §4.9.4.G 'Common parameters (all core tools)' at line 414 carries `explain` at line 421, 'On reads: return score/domain/hop trace (P12)'. The bad citation appeared in three places and all three are fixed to cite what exists: the header Parent line (dropped PR-4), the §1 Parent Requirement paragraph (now §4.5 step 3 for where the four stage values come from, plus §4.9.4.G `explain` for why a human-readable score trace may exist), and the §11 traceability table (row 1 now '§4.5 step 3', row 2 now '§4.9.4.G explain'). The correction also records, in the phase file, that the 'score is relative (rank fusion), not calibrated relevance' line is pre-existing renderer wording rather than a cited requirement, so this phase retains it as-is instead of claiming a requirement trace for it. The recommendation's second option was not taken: no new standing calibration rule was added to `requirement.md`, because AGENTS.md requires such an edit to be a consistency change across PR/FR/NFR, risks, and glossary, and no requirement text supports one. Nothing in the staged code violates a requirement, so no code changed for this finding. `grep -n 'PR-4' roadmap/phase-100660-cli-scores-breakdown.md` now returns nothing.

plan_dispositions.item: plan_unlimited[0]: extract the TEI doubles and pin the all-stages case through the CLI in both views
plan_dispositions.detail: New `crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read_tei_doubles_tests.rs` (265 lines) owns the bounded `POST /embed` and `POST /rerank` accept loops, the request caps, and the state factories, including a new `state_with_embedder_and_reranker` that attaches both fakes to one state. `cli_read_tests.rs:405` declares it as a sibling module (398 -> 405 lines). `cli_read_scores_tests.rs` drops the doubles and gains `recall_text_shows_every_populated_stage` (311 -> 424 lines), which seeds two items, drains the index through the fake embedder, and then checks the same hit with all four arms populated in the JSON view and in the text view. `semantic` and `reranker` are compared bit for bit against the payload; `keyword` is checked for presence, positivity, and non-rounded precision. This closes known limitation 1, which the first round had recorded as owed to a later phase because the file sat at 447 of 450 lines. Unlike the plan's suggestion of adding one text assertion to the existing reranker test, a new test was used: the existing test stops its double before its assertions, so a second recall there would hit a closed port. The new test keeps both doubles alive across the JSON call, the text call, and the assertions. The suggestion was also widened from 'reranker populated' to 'all four arms populated', which is what the item's own wording asks for and what the JSON view already supported.

plan_dispositions.item: plan_unlimited[1]: add a golden recall-text fixture shared by the renderer and CLI tests
plan_dispositions.disposition: partly done, remainder declined with reason
plan_dispositions.detail: The goal is met inside each test; the cross-crate sharing is not possible without a packaging change, and the reason is structural, not a matter of effort. Evidence: `crates/clio-lib/Cargo.toml:8-10` declares only `[[bin]] name = "clio", path = "src/main.rs"` and no `[lib]`, so the package has no library target. Every `crates/clio-lib/tests/*.rs` file is therefore its own crate and cannot `use` any item from the renderer or from the `#[cfg(test)]` modules inside `main.rs` (`cli_read_render_scores_tests` is declared at `main.rs:367`, and `cli_read_output_tests` at `main.rs:363`). A fixture shared between the renderer tests and the integration harnesses would have to be a plain text file pulled in with `include_str!`, but the two sides render different values (the renderer tests use hand-written payloads, the harnesses use real item ids and real scores), so the shared artifact could only be a placeholder template, and the code that fills the template in would still have to be written twice on the two sides of the crate boundary. Putting the matcher in the library instead would mean adding a `[lib]` target or a public test-only constant, which changes the published surface of the package; that is outside this phase's scope and is the kind of change the phase's own Scope Expansion Rule says to stop and request approval for. What was done instead: the new all-stages test parses each `scores: final ...` line into a `Breakdown` struct and asserts the full per-hit contract (all four stages present, exact values, no placeholder, headline agreement) rather than a scatter of substrings, so a layout change is one explicit diff. This limitation is recorded as known limitation 4 in the phase file. Deferred, with the packaging reason above, for whoever wants a public test-fixture convention.
